items.name: essay
items.title: Essay Module
items.description: Sidenotes + sticky TOC rail for long-form Essay pages: margin notes relocated into real DOM order, right after the paragraph that cites them, numbered by CSS counter and labeled `aria-label="Note N"` in the same order the counter advances — the mechanism that prevents the sidenote aria-label/DOM-order transcription bug found in the flagship migration (#89, williamzujkowski.github.io#380).

items.name: broadsheet
items.title: Broadsheet Pattern
items.description: The editorial Landing/archive pattern: masthead, lead article, numbered entry list, and post-header kicker. Entry numerals are generated from `data-entry-number` via `attr()`, never `counter()`, and every kicker/dateline row is the label voice: tracked capitals, because the default mono face has no small caps (`font-variant-caps: all-small-caps` only on a face with `smcp` + `c2sc`; remarque-audit checks).

items.name: forms
items.title: Forms Primitives
items.description: Native field/input/checkbox/radio/button primitives with state-color wiring. Every `.remarque-input` pairs `for`/`id` with its `.remarque-field-label`, and every `.remarque-field-message` is wired via `aria-describedby` on the control — the paint-layer `data-state` attribute is never the only signal; `aria-invalid`/`aria-describedby` on the input carry the real accessibility contract.

items.name: skip-link
items.title: Skip Link (chrome.css)
items.description: The first focusable element in <body>: `.remarque-skip-link` targets `<main id="main-content" tabindex="-1">`, visually hidden by clip-path (never an off-screen offset) until focused, then a filled fg-on-bg block on `--z-skip-link`. Ships with `.remarque-sr-only`. Shares chrome.css with the breadcrumb, pager and tags items.

items.name: breadcrumb
items.title: Breadcrumb (chrome.css)
items.description: The Reference/Docs breadcrumb kicker: `nav[aria-label="Breadcrumb"] > ol`, the current page last as `<span aria-current="page">` (never a link), separators generated by CSS with empty alt text and never typed into the DOM.

items.name: pager
items.title: Pager and Pagination (chrome.css)
items.description: Prev/next between adjacent pages with `rel="prev"`/`rel="next"`, an optional series row ("Part N of M" plus a <details> list with the current part `aria-current="page"`), and numbered `.remarque-pagination`. An endpoint with nowhere to go is omitted or plain text, never a disabled-looking link that stays focusable.

items.name: tags
items.title: Tags (chrome.css)
items.description: Tags as plain mono links in a `<ul>` with an accessible name, each `rel="tag"`. No border, fill or radius: an outlined or filled chip is a documented deviation, not personalization.

items.name: deck-picker
items.title: Palette Picker (chrome.css + remarque-tokens/deck)
items.description: A reader’s choice of color theme: a <details> holding a <fieldset> of native radio inputs (keyboard-operable with no ARIA-radio script), one per palette in deck.json plus value="" for the site’s own. Swatches are aria-hidden and colored by deck.css ([data-palette-swatch="<name>"]). Wire with deck.js bindPicker(); the module ships no script in this item.

items.name: palette-deck
items.title: Palette Deck (markup contract only — no executable content)
items.description: Markup/wiring contract for the Palette Deck: set `data-palette` on the same root element as `data-theme` and the two compose independently. This item ships ONLY that HTML fragment. `deck.js` — the runtime module itself, a dependency-free ~60-line ESM file — is deliberately NOT embedded here: the registry’s blocking no-executable-content condition is held to an unambiguous zero-`<script>`-tag bar across every item, so neither `deck.js` nor the FOUC-restore `<script>` sample documented alongside it in REMARQUE.md is included. Consume `deck.js` the normal way, via the `remarque-tokens/deck` package import (`dependencies` below); read the FOUC-restore snippet from the `docs` URL.
